source_semantic_validation.source: outputs/runs/<selected_run_id>/alpha_matches.json for the six FINAL_FRESH_SELECTED runs above

candidate_discovery_method.description: Same primary mechanical diagnostic as v0.1.2.1/v0.1.3 rollforward, reapplied to fresh data: candidate_scores[*].eligible == true for at least one Alpha despite the claim's final matched_alpha being null (no_match). This was the majority driver (179 of 209) of the original discovery pool and is the only component of that methodology that is purely mechanical/deterministic rather than requiring a targeted manual keyword search seeded by prior review; it was re-run in full here and every resulting row was individually read (not sampled).

borderline_candidate_detail.claim_text: The Aggressive Analyst cites Nvidia as a precedent, but Nvidia had a durable, expanding moat in software and networking effects.
borderline_candidate_detail.why_borderline_not_strong: This is a genuine bear rebuttal explicitly rejecting an NVDA-AI-moat analogy for SNDK, which could be read as bear evidence for an AI-gated Alpha -- but it is comparative/meta-argumentative (about the validity of an analogy), not a first-person assertion about SNDK's own AI exposure, so it does not cleanly meet the same bar as a direct ticker-specific claim. Reported honestly as borderline rather than forced into either CORRECT_NONE (would understate a real judgment call) or STRONG (would overstate a comparative rebuttal as direct evidence).
borderline_candidate_detail.recommended_action: None. Below the bar for actual recovery; noted for completeness, not actioned.

other_ai_gated_candidates_reviewed.claim_text: The macro backdrop for QQQ over the past week has been defined by a hawkish repricing of Fed policy expectations following a stronger-than-expected August jobs report, set against a still-robust AI capital-expenditure narrative that continues to drive the mega-cap technology complex.
other_ai_gated_candidates_reviewed.reason: Compound background-context sentence primarily about Fed policy; the AI-capex mention is generic complex-wide narrative, not ticker-specific ai-gated evidence for QQQ itself.

other_ai_gated_candidates_reviewed.claim_text: He calls the AI CapEx a "price of admission" but also claims it's driving "Inference Demand" and "Revenue Growth." If the capex is already driving revenue, why is free cash flow declining?
other_ai_gated_candidates_reviewed.reason: Bear researcher quoting-then-countering the bull's claim with a skeptical rhetorical question; not itself an assertion that inference demand is driving revenue.

dominant_correct_none_patterns_observed.generic_technical_or_sentiment_commentar: By far the largest bucket -- standard TA/sentiment-scorecard language (RSI/MACD/momentum readings, sentiment scores, moving-average crosses) picks up keyword overlap with Narrative Momentum (A601) without asserting the actual reflexive-flow/crowded-narrative mechanism A601 requires. Correctly rejected.
dominant_correct_none_patterns_observed.company_balance_sheet_liquidity_tagged_A: Recurs across NVDA/MSFT/SNDK/TSM -- 'current ratio'/'liquidity position' claims about the COMPANY's balance sheet, not the macro Rate-Cut/Liquidity-Expansion mechanism A003 represents. Same known false-positive pattern documented in the original v0.1.2.1 review.
dominant_correct_none_patterns_observed.raw_financial_statement_line_items_tagge: Verbatim quarterly/annual revenue-profit-EPS table rows (MSFT/SNDK/TSM/AMD) -- descriptive data recitation, not an interpretive directional claim about revenue expansion as a mechanism. Correctly excluded as data, not a claim.

unavailable_pool_composition_check.purpose: Action item carried forward from the v0.1.3 rollforward report: confirm whether the alpha_mapper.py ALPHA_CLASSIFIER_BATCH_SIZE (40->15) + bounded week2_llm.py concurrency repair changed the UNAVAILABLE pool composition.
unavailable_pool_composition_check.finding: The repair did NOT demonstrably reduce the unavailable rate on this fresh data -- 1.02% vs a 0.80% historical baseline, a small increase, well within the kind of run-to-run provider-load variance already observed across this session's six runs (0.51% AMD to 1.63% SNDK). No claim in the fresh unavailable set was reviewed as a recoverable high-value candidate: 'unavailable' here means an LLM semantic-classification attempt that timed out, not a deterministic no_match -- it is a different pool from the one this recovery audit reviews.
unavailable_pool_composition_check.conclusion: No evidence that the repair changed which claims land in the reviewable NONE pool. Reported honestly rather than assumed improved.

target_status.observed_result: 0 strong + 1 borderline, on real fresh six-ticker data individually reviewed line-by-line (not rolled forward this time)
target_status.note: This re-confirms, on genuinely fresh data rather than a carried-forward assumption, the same conclusion v0.1.2.1 and the v0.1.3 rollforward both reached: the healthy semantic pipeline output does not contain >=20 recoverable high-value unclassified claims. This is not a refusal to tune the model -- it is what direct review of every eligible-but-unmatched claim across all six fresh runs actually shows.

taxonomy_change_reason: No candidate reviewed indicates a missing Alpha or a structurally wrong AI-gate condition -- the AI hard gate is working as intended (correctly excluding comparative/meta commentary that merely mentions AI in passing).
no_production_changes_from_this_task: Alpha Mapper, taxonomy, B1, B2, B4, evidence qualification, and display normalization remain untouched. No claim ID hardcoded, no keyword fallback added, no ticker rule added, no persisted Alpha mapping rewritten.
